latest_release.name: AgentDeck npm v2.1.5
latest_release.body:
## AgentDeck npm v2.1.5

- **OpenCode 2.x.** Standalone OpenCode 2.x sessions are observed again. 2.x
  rejected the previous observer plugin at load, so no session reached
  AgentDeck and the process scan showed an extra idle session named after the
  home folder. Observer plugin v8 loads under 2.x and 1.x. Reinstall it with
  `agentdeck daemon install`, then restart OpenCode once. The Mac app updates
  an observer it installed when it starts, unless the file was edited
  ([#836](https://github.com/puritysb/AgentDeck/pull/836)). Approvals from a
  device work on 2.x; questions stay display-only there.
  [#832](https://github.com/puritysb/AgentDeck/pull/832)
- **Background work for OpenCode and Antigravity.** OpenCode 2.x background
  shells and subagents, and Antigravity background commands, count as
  background work. A background `gh run watch` shows as a CI wait, as it does
  for Claude Code and Codex. Node and Mac daemons.
  [#832](https://github.com/puritysb/AgentDeck/pull/832)
- **Antigravity project names.** A conversation is named after its own
  workspace folder. An older conversation still running in a folder showed
  as "Antigravity". Node and Mac daemons.
  [#834](https://github.com/puritysb/AgentDeck/pull/834)
- **Deck keys (Stream Deck, D200H).** Two Claude Code sessions in one project
  read `epoch-of-tech #c4fe` instead of a second line of `-89 #c4fe`.
  [#834](https://github.com/puritysb/AgentDeck/pull/834)
- **Creature colors.** Antigravity draws its colored mark instead of a gray one
  on the iDotMatrix, the Timebox and the IPS10 workspace. An off-duty Dot shows
  a dimmed pearl on the Pixoo and matrix displays instead of a gray saucer
  shape. [#833](https://github.com/puritysb/AgentDeck/pull/833)
- **Android over USB.** The Node daemon alone owns the dashboard's ADB reverse
  tunnels and repairs a stale mapping when a reserved USB device returns.
  [#824](https://github.com/puritysb/AgentDeck/pull/824) (npm only)
- **Vobot over TLS.** The Node daemon also delivers display power and dimming
  state to compatible devices with the display-state permission, as the Mac
  app did in 2.2.2. [#820](https://github.com/puritysb/AgentDeck/pull/820) (npm only)

The CLI, daemon, and Claude Code / Codex / OpenCode hook installers.
Optional — the macOS App Store app runs standalone without any of this.

### Install
```bash
npx @agentdeck/setup
```

### Packages
| Package | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `@agentdeck/setup` | One-command installer |
| `@agentdeck/bridge` | `agentdeck` CLI — daemon hub + session bridge |
| `@agentdeck/hooks` | Agent lifecycle hook installers |
| `@agentdeck/shared` | Shared protocol types and layout engines |

Full changelog: https://github.com/puritysb/AgentDeck/blob/npm-v2.1.5/CHANGELOG.md

detail.readme:
# AgentDeck

**Your AI agents, at a glance. Across your desk.** AgentDeck brings your AI agents into one local dashboard. See which are working, waiting for you, or finished—across projects and tools. Watch them in a living aquarium, follow the timeline, and keep usage limits in view. Use your Mac or terminal on its own, or add a tablet, Stream Deck, e-ink reader, or small desk display.

*Photographed on September 28, 2026. [See the full desk](docs/media/desk-overview.jpg).* **Start with what you already have. No extra hardware required.** Use your Mac or terminal on its own, then add the displays that fit your desk. [**Get started →**](#start-here) · [**Choose your view ↓**](#choose-your-view) · [Watch the hardware desk tour](https://youtu.be/s-f8ICBcC4o)

▶ Watch the AgentDeck product tour  ·  🌊 Project website  ·  Devices  ·  Live preview  ·  Design system

## AgentDeck · 2.0 product tour [![AgentDeck product tour: sessions, collaboration, usage, real answers, evaluation and devices](docs/media/current/agentdeck-200-product-tour-preview.gif)](https://puritysb.github.io/AgentDeck/#product-tour) A **2 minute 24 second** tour of the whole workflow: parallel agent sessions, per-session history and CI waiting, collaboration, usage windows, original choices and one-time approval, voice and native agent controls, task evaluation and recorded evidence, then the roles of keypads, tablets, e-ink and small displays. Actual Mac/iPad UI and production renderers use fictional activity; the phone control chapter uses a real local OpenCode execution. Static captures and older hardware photographs are labeled in the video. It was recorded on 2.0 builds, with English, Korean and Japanese captions; released downloads retain their channel versions. CloudKit/Watch remains a separate development experiment. [Watch the captioned product tour](https://puritysb.github.io/AgentDeck/#product-tour) · [Choice and approval detail](https://puritysb.github.io/AgentDeck/#controller-workflow) · [Aquarium detail](https://puritysb.github.io/AgentDeck/#current-habitat) · [Device captures](https://puritysb.github.io/AgentDeck/hardware/#current-captures) · [Media provenance](docs/media/current/manifest.json) Historical photographs and earlier recordings remain available. The device gallery labels its AI-assisted photo composite separately from actual app and firmware captures. ## Start here **No extra hardware required.** Choose a native dashboard or the terminal path. ### Mac, iPhone, iPad, and Apple Watch [Install from the App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6784822497?pt=128040795&ct=github-readme-202610&mt=8). The Mac app includes its own daemon and needs no Node.js. Enable your agent integrations in Settings, then run your agents normally. Pair iPhone or iPad with the local daemon for live sessions and supported controls. With AgentDeck 2.2.0, you can also enable **Remote monitoring** on a Mac and read its activity over private iCloud on iPhone, iPad, and Apple Watch using the same Apple Account. [Set up Remote monitoring](docs/apple-app.md#remote-monitoring-via-icloud). Requires macOS 26+, iOS/iPadOS 17+, or watchOS 10+ for the included Watch app. ### Terminal, Windows, Linux, and external integrations Requires Node.js **22, 24, or 26** and a supported agent on macOS 15+, [Windows 11](docs/windows.md), or [Linux](docs/linux.md). ```bash npx @agentdeck/setup agentdeck daemon install # refresh hooks and start observation claude # or: codex · opencode · kiro-cli ``` In another terminal: ```bash agentdeck dashboard # live sessions, aquarium, usage, and timeline ``` The Mac app can also attach to the CLI daemon for additional integrations, including Claude subscription gauges and ADB device support. [Compare capabilities](docs/appstore-feature-matrix.md). For setup problems, run `agentdeck diag agents` or see [installation](docs/install.md) and [troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md).
Existing managed sessions and remote attach `agentdeck claude`, `agentdeck codex`, `agentdeck opencode`, and `agentdeck monitor` are a long-term compatibility path; no removal is planned. Ordinary local sessions should use the daemon with normal agent commands. Daemon-first equivalents exist for launch arguments (`agentdeck run`), deck ordering (`agentdeck order`) and remote sessions (`agentdeck relay`, experimental). Immediate terminal steering stays managed-only. See the [CLI reference](docs/cli.md), [remote attach guide](docs/daemon.md#remote-attach-cross-machine-sessions), and [decision record](docs/managed-replacement-inventory.md#october-15-decision).
## Choose your view Start with your Mac or terminal; add screens and controls as needed. Mobile apps and hardware connect to a daemon on your computer. | Surface | What it offers | Setup | |---|---|---| | Mac · iPhone · iPad | Native dashboard and 3D aquarium; Mac includes the daemon | [Apple guide](docs/apple-app.md) | | Terminal | Sessions, braille aquarium, usage and timeline | [TUI guide](docs/tui-dashboard.md) | | Android tablet or e-ink reader | A dedicated companion dashboard | [Android guide](docs/android.md) | | Stream Deck · Ulanzi | Physical session keys and supported controls | [Stream Deck](docs/streamdeck-layout.md) · [Ulanzi](docs/devices.md) | | ESP32 · TRMNL | Compact panels, rotary controls and e-ink status boards | [Firmware guide](docs/esp32.md) | | Pixoo · TC001 · Timebox · iDotMatrix | Agent status on pixel displays | [Device guide](docs/devices.md) | | Vobot Mini Dock | Live session and Claude and Codex usage display on a trusted LAN. The development build adds full-screen input alerts and a pulsing rear LED | [Vobot guide](integrations/vobot/README.md) · [Device photo](https://puritysb.github.io/AgentDeck/hardware/#vobot-mini-dock) | Controls require a supported session control path; other surfaces show status. D200X support covers LCD keys, not encoders. See the [hardware compatibility matrix](docs/hardware-compatibility.md) for model-specific limits. [**Browse device photos and live previews →**](https://puritysb.github.io/AgentDeck/hardware/) ## A dashboard that feels alive **On your Mac, no extra hardware required.** Watch the native app in action below.

Choose the familiar dashboard or the **native 3D aquarium** on Mac, iPhone/iPad, and Android LCD devices. Each session becomes a creature; its activity changes its movement, and nearby fish react. On mobile, tap empty water to hide the panels and move closer. Tap again to return. Existing preferences are preserved. The preview above shows fictional activity in the real native app; no private workspace data is shown. [Watch the current aquarium recording](https://puritysb.github.io/AgentDeck/#current-habitat) or take the [hardware desk tour](https://youtu.be/s-f8ICBcC4o). ## What it does - **Follow parallel work.** Session names, current tools, and a shared timeline explain what each agent is doing. On Mac, [Work](docs/apple-app.md#work-on-mac) shows reported subagents, background jobs, and confirmed message deliveries. - **Notice when you are needed.** Permission and input requests stand out. Answer or interrupt from supported surfaces when the session provides a real control path; otherwise prompts are display-only. - **Keep usage visible.** Claude, Codex, and z.ai/GLM gauges appear where the connected provider supplies usage data. Agent identity and model provider remain separate. - **Choose your display.** The 3D scene keeps up to eight foreground residents readable while the roster retains every session. E-ink uses a static rendered backdrop and restrained motion; compact panels keep their focused layouts. ## Agents AgentDeck is growing beyond coding workflows: **Hermes Agent** is supported as an opt-in preview (see the table). The table below lists current integrations and how each is observed. | Agent | Observation | |---|---| | **Claude Code** | Lifecycle hooks; primary supported integration | | **Codex CLI** | Lifecycle hooks and rollout logs | | **Codex Desktop** | Observed on macOS; Windows verification pending | | **OpenCode** | Observer plugin and native events | | **Kiro CLI / IDE** | Transcript observation; delayed, idle-only activity | | **Antigravity** | Passive observation through the CLI daemon | | **OpenClaw** | Experimental Gateway integration | | **Hermes Agent** | Preview: opt-in observer plugin (`agentdeck hermes-observer`, then `hermes plugins enable agentdeck-observer`); read-only | Run agents normally; AgentDeck reads their native events rather than scraping terminal screens. Kiro has no managed launcher, and the sandboxed Mac app needs a one-time folder grant for its transcripts. Detailed setup and limitations: [configuration](docs/configuration.md), [Apple guide](docs/apple-app.md), and [Gateway guide](docs/gateway-protocol.md). ## Releases ### Compatibility and delivery channels Use the channel for your device. Components with the same major version work together; target-specific updates can ship at different times. [Delivery records](RELEASING.md) distinguish published downloads, Store listings and pending review, with the date each was checked. | Product | Install / update | Release tag | |---|---|---| | Mac · iPhone · iPad · Apple Watch | [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6784822497?pt=128040795&ct=github-readme-202610&mt=8) | `apple-v*` | | Android tablets and e-ink | [Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=dev.agentdeck) · [signed GitHub APK](https://github.com/puritysb/AgentDeck/releases?q=android-v&expanded=true) | `android-v*` | | CLI + daemon | [`npx @agentdeck/setup`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@agentdeck/setup) | `npm-v*` | | Stream Deck / Mini / XL / Plus / + XL | [Elgato Marketplace](https://marketplace.elgato.com/product/agentdeck-dce3806b-176e-40f2-be7d-e029bec0f464) | `streamdeck-v*` | | Ulanzi D200H / D200X LCD keys | [Ulanzi Marketplace](https://ugc.ulanzistudio.com/contentView/1239890184745660416); D200X encoders are not supported | `ulanzi-v*` | | Vobot Mini Dock | [Wi-Fi pairing](integrations/vobot/README.md#pair-over-wi-fi) on stock firmware 1.2.6 or later | [Gallery 0.3.0 approved](integrations/vobot/README.md#gallery-release) | | ESP32 panels and TRMNL 7.5" | [Browser flasher](https://puritysb.github.io/AgentDeck/flash/) · [firmware releases](https://github.com/puritysb/AgentDeck/releases?q=esp32-v&expanded=true) | `esp32-v*` | Update Android through your existing signing channel: Play and GitHub APK signatures can differ. Supported ESP32 boards offer Wi-Fi OTA after the first USB flash. See the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md), [all releases](https://github.com/puritysb/AgentDeck/releases), and [version policy](RELEASING.md#choosing-a-version). ## Compatible Companion Projects Independent integrations have their own releases and support. Both projects below are **Community** integrations; listing does not imply verified compatibility. - [Pocket Daily Reader](https://github.com/puritysb/pocket-daily-reader): an offline-first reader using the `portable-reader/v1` profile. - [Bitfocus Companion module](https://github.com/houtacheng/companion-module-agentdeck) by [@houtacheng](https://github.com/houtacheng): session tiles, controls, and usage through `companion-control/v1`. See the [Surface Protocol](docs/surface-protocol.md) for capabilities, runtime status, integration manifests, and conformance levels. ## Documentation **Start with the website** — [puritysb.github.io/AgentDeck](https://puritysb.github.io/AgentDeck/) carries the rendered device catalog, live renderer previews, the design system, and build health. | | | |---|---| | **Using it** | [CLI reference](docs/cli.md) · [Configuration](docs/configuration.md) · [Troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md) · [Windows](docs/windows.md) · [Linux](docs/linux.md) | | **Surfaces** | [Hardware matrix](docs/hardware-compatibility.md) · [Stream Deck layout](docs/streamdeck-layout.md) · [Devices](docs/devices.md) · [ESP32](docs/esp32.md) · [Android](docs/android.md) · [Apple](docs/apple-app.md) · [TUI](docs/tui-dashboard.md) | | **Internals** | [Architecture](docs/architecture.md) · [Surface protocol](docs/surface-protocol.md) · [Internal bridge protocol](docs/protocol.md) · [Daemon](docs/daemon.md) · [Gateway protocol](docs/gateway-protocol.md) · [Testing](docs/testing.md) | | **Evaluation** | [Why APME](docs/why-apme.md) · [APME](docs/apme.md) · [Pipeline](docs/apme-pipeline.md) | | **Design** | [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md) · [Tokens](design/tokens.css) · [Resource map](design/RESOURCES.md) | | **Project** | [Roadmap](docs/roadmap.md) · [Releasing](RELEASING.md) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) · [Agent harness](docs/agent-harness.md) · [AI-assisted maintenance](docs/ai-assisted-maintenance.md) | ## Automated security checks [![Security scan](https://github.com/puritysb/AgentDeck/actions/workflows/security-scan.yml/badge.svg?branch=master)](https://github.com/puritysb/AgentDeck/actions/workflows/security-scan.yml?query=branch%3Amaster) [![CodeQL analysis](https://github.com/puritysb/AgentDeck/actions/workflows/codeql.yml/badge.svg?branch=master)](https://github.com/puritysb/AgentDeck/actions/workflows/codeql.yml?query=branch%3Amaster) [![Snyk monthly comparison](https://github.com/puritysb/AgentDeck/actions/workflows/snyk-monthly.yml/badge.svg?branch=master)](https://github.com/puritysb/AgentDeck/actions/workflows/snyk-monthly.yml) [![Security pipeline health](https://github.com/puritysb/AgentDeck/actions/workflows/security-health.yml/badge.svg?branch=master)](https://github.com/puritysb/AgentDeck/actions/workflows/security-health.yml?query=branch%3Amaster) Dependency audits and pairing-token detection run on PRs, `master` pushes and daily. CodeQL adds source analysis; Snyk provides a monthly comparison, and an hourly watchdog checks scan freshness. PR dependency review flags newly introduced high/critical advisories. **Badges show workflow status, not a vulnerability-free certification.** CodeQL can complete with alerts; Snyk can complete with findings recorded for review. The report preserves each run's commit, date, scope and limitations. [Results and coverage](https://puritysb.github.io/AgentDeck/reports/#verify) · [Security scanning runbook](docs/security-scanning.md) · [Report a vulnerability privately](SECURITY.md) ## Development ```bash pnpm install && pnpm build pnpm -r --parallel dev pnpm test ``` [Build from source](docs/install.md) · [Testing](docs/testing.md) · [Build health](https://puritysb.github.io/AgentDeck/reports/). Coding agents should start at [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). ## Community Bug reports, hardware verification, documentation fixes, and focused pull requests are welcome. Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md), use [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) for private vulnerability reports, and follow the [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). See [AI-assisted maintenance](docs/ai-assisted-maintenance.md) for how maintainers review agent-assisted work. ## License & attribution MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE). Independent project.
